title: East Uusimaa: 0.3 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €15,600 a year
markdown:
# East Uusimaa: 0.3 more lung cancer patients a year treated to cure, for €15,600 a year

> 0.3 more patients a year treated to cure · €15,600 of €1M · €984,400 left: nothing more pays off on today's evidence

## The gap

Of 100 lung cancer patients in East Uusimaa, 28 get treatment that aims to cure. In Finland it is 27. The difference is within what chance alone gives a county of this size. [^care_curative] Compared with the best quarter of counties (30.4% treated to cure), about 1.1 patients a year are missing, range 0.0 to 4.0 [^care_curative] [^model]. Against Finland as a whole there is no measured shortfall to split between surgery and radiotherapy [^care_curative] [^model]. The share is about what the age of the county's residents predicts, 27.2% [^model].

## The target

Raise the share of lung cancer patients treated to cure from 28.3% to 28.8% by 2028: 0.3 more patients a year (range 0.0–0.6), for €15,600 a year, about €57,778 per extra patient. [^care_curative][^model]

## Funded actions

| # | Action and owner | Cost a year | More patients treated to cure a year (range) | First step this week | Measure: today → target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | **The county can start on Monday** | | | | |
| 1 | **Fitness assessment and prehabilitation before deciding against curative treatment**[^ev_prehab_fitness_assessment_1]. Chief physician of pulmonology; leads of rehabilitation and geriatrics | €15,600 | 0.3 (0.0–0.6) | Decide that no stage I-III patient is recorded as "not fit" without an exercise test, and book the physiotherapy group. | Share of patients who get treatment that aims to cure: 28.3% → 28.8% by 2028 |
| | **Total** | **€15,600** | **0.3 (0.0–0.6)** | | |

No trial has measured these effects; the low end of every range is zero. The ranges do not add up to the range of the total, because the measures share one ceiling. Costs are assumptions. [^model]

## Needs a national decision (outside this budget)

- **Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers**[^ev_ldct_screening_1]: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health and Palko (decision), Finnish Cancer Registry (steering), county (delivery). €318,752 a year; modelled to avoid 0.5 deaths a year (0.1–1.4). Not counted in this budget. Not a county decision. Ask the Ministry and Palko for the timetable after the 2026-2028 pilot and offer the county as a pilot site. [^model]

## What to measure from Monday

- Share of patients treated to cure: 28.3% (2019–2023, measured) → 28.8% by 2028. [^care_curative][^model]
- The registry's public figures cover 2019–2023; count these each month from the county's own records. [^care_curative]

## What more money buys, and what it cannot

The remaining €984,400 buys nothing more in the model: access measures are limited by the reachable part of the measured shortfall, not by money [^model]. To see what else the money could do, look at low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers, which needs a national decision, or rank measures by deaths avoided instead [^model]. Lung cancer causes about 48 deaths a year in East Uusimaa; this plan is modelled to avoid 0.0 of them (0.0-0.2) [^deaths] [^model].

## Limits

- Effects are assumptions, not trial results: each range runs from all assumptions at their lowest to all at their highest, and is not a probability [^model].
- Shares are adjusted only for residents' age, not stage at diagnosis, other illness, histology, smoking or recording; county figures cannot show cause [^model].
- The estimated symptom-to-treatment clock is not used here: a check against 3 measured outcomes confirmed none of them [^model].
